nodes.name: Subatomic Particles
nodes.description: Protons, neutrons, and electrons making up the atom, whose relative masses and charges determine atomic number, mass number, and chemical behaviour.

nodes.name: Isotopes
nodes.description: Atoms of the same element with equal protons but different numbers of neutrons, giving different mass numbers but identical chemical properties.

nodes.name: Electronic Configuration
nodes.description: The arrangement of electrons in shells, subshells, and orbitals following the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule, and the Pauli exclusion principle.
nodes.visual_hint: Orbital filling diagram across shells and subshells.

nodes.name: Atomic Orbital Shapes
nodes.description: The shapes and orientations of atomic orbitals, including spherical s orbitals, directional p orbitals and the prescribed 3dxy and 3dz² orbitals, represented as probability regions rather than electron paths.
nodes.visual_hint: Show labelled s, p, 3dxy and 3dz² probability-density shapes and orientations.

nodes.name: Ionisation Energy
nodes.description: The energy required to remove electrons from gaseous atoms, whose successive values and periodic trends provide evidence for electronic structure.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot successive ionisation energies revealing shell structure.

nodes.name: Relative Atomic, Molecular and Formula Masses
nodes.description: The unified atomic mass unit is one twelfth of a carbon-12 atom's mass; relative isotopic, atomic, molecular and formula masses compare the relevant mass with this reference and are dimensionless.

nodes.name: The Mole and Avogadro Constant
nodes.name_zh: 摩尔与阿伏伽德罗常数
nodes.description: The mole as the amount containing Avogadro's number of particles, linking number of particles, mass, and molar quantities in calculations.

nodes.name: Empirical and Molecular Formulae
nodes.description: Empirical formulae give the simplest whole-number atom ratio and molecular formulae give the actual numbers. Formula notation also distinguishes anhydrous and hydrated salts and records water of crystallisation in a hydrate.

nodes.name: Reacting Masses and Gas Volumes
nodes.description: Using balanced equations and the mole concept to calculate reacting masses, gas volumes, and theoretical yields in stoichiometric problems.

nodes.name: Concentration and Titration
nodes.description: Determining unknown concentrations by titration, using the mole ratio in a balanced equation and an indicated end point to calculate the result.

nodes.name: Ionic Bonding
nodes.description: Bonding by electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer, producing giant ionic lattices with high melting points.
nodes.visual_hint: Dot-and-cross diagram of electron transfer forming ions.

nodes.name: Covalent Bonding
nodes.description: Covalent bonding is electrostatic attraction involving shared electron pairs, including single, double, triple and dative bonds. Direct orbital overlap forms σ bonds, sideways p-orbital overlap forms π bonds, and sp, sp² and sp³ hybridisation explains bond arrangement and molecular shape.
nodes.visual_hint: Dot-and-cross diagram of shared electron pairs.

nodes.name: Metallic Bonding
nodes.description: Bonding in metals as a lattice of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, explaining conductivity, malleability, and high melting points.

nodes.name: Shapes of Molecules (VSEPR)
nodes.description: Predicting molecular shapes and bond angles using valence-shell electron-pair repulsion, where electron pairs arrange to minimise mutual repulsion.
nodes.visual_hint: Rotate 3D molecular shapes showing bond angles for each electron-pair geometry.

nodes.name: Electronegativity and Polarity
nodes.description: The tendency of an atom to attract a shared electron pair, whose differences create bond polarity and overall molecular dipoles.

nodes.name: Intermolecular Forces
nodes.description: Forces between molecules—van der Waals, permanent dipole-dipole, and hydrogen bonding—that determine physical properties such as boiling point.

nodes.name: Kinetic Model and Ideal Gas Behaviour
nodes.name_zh: 气体动理论模型与理想气体行为
nodes.description: Gas pressure arises from molecular collisions with container walls and the associated momentum changes. Ideal-gas particles have negligible volume and no intermolecular attraction, leading to the equation pV = nRT.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot pV = nRT relationships between pressure, volume, and temperature.

nodes.name: Solid Structures
nodes.description: Giant ionic, giant covalent, simple molecular, and metallic solid structures, whose bonding and arrangement determine their physical properties.

nodes.name: Enthalpy Changes
nodes.description: Enthalpy changes of reactions measured at constant pressure, including standard enthalpies of formation, combustion, and reaction.
nodes.visual_hint: Energy-profile diagram of enthalpy change with activation energy.

nodes.name: Hess's Law
nodes.description: Hess's law stating that the enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the route taken, allowing indirect calculation via energy cycles.
nodes.visual_hint: Hess-cycle diagram of alternative reaction routes.

nodes.name: Bond Enthalpy and Bond Length
nodes.description: Bond enthalpy is the energy required to break one mole of a particular covalent bond in gaseous molecules, while bond length is the internuclear distance between bonded atoms; shorter, stronger bonds are generally harder to break and help explain differences in molecular reactivity.

nodes.name: Calorimetry
nodes.description: Measuring enthalpy changes experimentally from temperature changes using the relationship q equals mcΔT in a calorimeter.

nodes.name: Rate of Reaction
nodes.description: The rate of reaction as the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time, and the factors that affect it.

nodes.name: Collision Theory
nodes.description: Collision theory explaining rates through the frequency of collisions and the proportion exceeding the activation energy with correct orientation.

nodes.name: Maxwell-Boltzmann Distribution
nodes.description: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of molecular energies, used to explain the effect of temperature and catalysts on reaction rate.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot the Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution and the effect of temperature and catalyst.

nodes.name: Catalysis
nodes.description: Catalysts increasing reaction rate by providing an alternative pathway of lower activation energy, classified as homogeneous or heterogeneous.

nodes.name: Rate Equations and Orders
nodes.description: Rate equations relating rate to reactant concentrations raised to their orders, with the rate constant determined experimentally.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot reaction rate against concentration for zero, first, and second order.

nodes.name: Rate-Determining Step
nodes.description: The rate-determining step as the slowest step in a mechanism, whose reactants appear in the experimentally determined rate equation.

nodes.name: Dynamic Equilibrium
nodes.description: Dynamic equilibrium in a closed system where the forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates and concentrations remain constant.

nodes.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
nodes.description: Le Chatelier's principle predicting how an equilibrium position shifts to oppose changes in concentration, pressure, or temperature.
nodes.visual_hint: Shift an equilibrium with sliders for concentration, pressure, and temperature.

nodes.name: Equilibrium Constants Kc and Kp
nodes.name_zh: 平衡常数 Kc 与 Kp
nodes.description: Equilibrium constants Kc and Kp expressing the position of equilibrium in terms of concentrations or partial pressures at a given temperature.

nodes.name: Brønsted-Lowry Theory
nodes.description: The Brønsted-Lowry theory defining acids as proton donors and bases as proton acceptors, related through conjugate acid-base pairs.

nodes.name: Strong and Weak Acids
nodes.description: The distinction between strong acids that fully dissociate and weak acids that only partially dissociate in aqueous solution.

nodes.name: pH and Acid Dissociation Constant
nodes.description: The pH scale measuring hydrogen-ion concentration and the acid dissociation constant Ka quantifying the strength of a weak acid.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot a titration pH curve and locate the equivalence point.

nodes.name: Buffers
nodes.description: Buffer solutions resisting pH change on adding small amounts of acid or base, formed from a weak acid and its conjugate base.

nodes.name: Solubility Product
nodes.description: The solubility product Ksp as the equilibrium constant for a sparingly soluble salt dissolving, predicting precipitation and the common-ion effect.

nodes.name: Partition Coefficient
nodes.description: At equilibrium, a partition coefficient is the specified ratio of concentrations of the same physical-state solute in two immiscible solvents; it is calculated using a consistent ratio and explained by solute-solvent polarity.

nodes.name: Oxidation Numbers
nodes.description: Oxidation numbers assigned by rules to track electron transfer, identifying which species are oxidised and reduced in a redox reaction.

nodes.name: Redox Equations
nodes.description: Constructing balanced redox equations by combining oxidation and reduction half-equations so that electrons gained equal electrons lost.

nodes.name: Electrode Potentials
nodes.description: Standard electrode potentials measuring a half-cell's tendency to gain electrons relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

nodes.name: Electrochemical Cells
nodes.description: Electrochemical cells generating an EMF from two half-cells, with the cell potential calculated from standard electrode potentials.

nodes.name: Electrolysis
nodes.description: The decomposition of molten or aqueous compounds by passing electricity, with products predicted from electrode reactions and Faraday's laws.

nodes.name: Lattice Energy and Born-Haber Cycles
nodes.name_zh: 晶格能与玻恩-哈伯循环
nodes.description: Born-Haber cycles applying Hess's law to determine lattice energy from enthalpies of formation, atomisation, ionisation, and electron affinity.
nodes.visual_hint: Born-Haber cycle diagram of the lattice-energy enthalpy steps.

nodes.name: Entropy
nodes.description: Entropy as a measure of the disorder of a system, with spontaneous change tending toward increased total entropy.

nodes.name: Gibbs Free Energy
nodes.description: Gibbs free energy combines enthalpy and entropy, with negative ΔG indicating thermodynamic feasibility. For an electrochemical reaction, standard free energy and standard cell potential are connected by ΔG° = -nFE°cell.

nodes.name: Periodic Trends
nodes.description: Trends across periods and down groups in atomic radius, ionisation energy, and electronegativity, explained by nuclear charge and shielding.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot periodic trends in atomic radius and ionisation energy across a period.

nodes.name: Period 3 Elements and Oxides
nodes.description: The properties of Period 3 elements and their oxides and chlorides, showing the trend from metallic to covalent character.

nodes.name: Group 2 Chemistry
nodes.description: The chemistry of Group 2 metals, including reactions with water and oxygen and trends in reactivity and thermal stability of compounds.

nodes.name: Group 17 Halogens
nodes.description: The chemistry of Group 17 halogens includes trends in volatility and oxidising power, displacement reactions, and chlorine water purification, where chlorine forms the active species HOCl and ClO− that kill bacteria.

nodes.name: Nitrogen and Sulfur
nodes.description: The chemistry of nitrogen and sulfur, including ammonia, the oxides of nitrogen and sulfur, and their environmental significance.

nodes.name: Transition Element Properties
nodes.description: Characteristic properties of transition elements, including variable oxidation states, catalytic activity, coloured ions, and complex formation.

nodes.name: Complex Ions and Ligands
nodes.description: Complex ions formed by a central metal ion bonded to ligands through dative covalent bonds, with characteristic coordination numbers and shapes.

nodes.name: Colour and Catalysis
nodes.description: The origin of colour in transition-metal complexes from d-orbital splitting, and their use as homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts.

nodes.name: Functional Groups and Organic Representations
nodes.name_zh: 官能团与有机结构表示
nodes.description: Functional groups determine characteristic physical and chemical properties and reactions; the same organic structure can be interpreted and converted among general, structural, displayed and skeletal formulae.

nodes.name: Nomenclature
nodes.description: The systematic IUPAC naming of organic compounds based on chain length, functional groups, and the positions of substituents.

nodes.name: Isomerism
nodes.description: Structural isomerism and stereoisomerism, including cis-trans and optical isomers, arising from different arrangements of the same atoms.

nodes.name: Bond Fission and Reactive Species
nodes.description: Homolytic bond fission produces free radicals, species with one or more unpaired electrons, while heterolytic bond fission produces ions; both generate reactive species in organic mechanisms.

nodes.name: Reaction Mechanism Types
nodes.description: Classifying organic reactions as substitution, addition, and elimination, with curly-arrow notation representing the movement of electron pairs.

nodes.name: Alkanes
nodes.description: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with single carbon-carbon bonds. Their chemistry includes combustion, free-radical halogen substitution and catalytic cracking of heavy fractions into lower-Mr alkanes and alkenes.

nodes.name: Alkenes
nodes.description: Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing a carbon-carbon double bond, undergoing electrophilic addition and characterised by their greater reactivity.

nodes.name: Addition Polymerisation
nodes.description: Addition polymerisation joins alkene monomers into carbon-chain polymers. Poly(alkenes) are difficult to biodegrade because their backbones are chemically inert, while some polymers can be designed or modified to undergo light-initiated chain scission and fragmentation.

nodes.name: Nucleophilic Substitution
nodes.description: Halogenoalkanes are classified as primary, secondary or tertiary by the carbon bearing the halogen. Nucleophilic substitution replaces the halogen through SN2, SN1 or mixed pathways whose tendency depends on that structure.

nodes.name: Elimination Reactions
nodes.description: Elimination reactions of halogenoalkanes removing a hydrogen halide to form an alkene, competing with nucleophilic substitution.

nodes.name: Alcohols and Their Reactions
nodes.description: Alcohol reactions include combustion, substitution to halogenoalkanes, dehydration to alkenes and esterification. Alcohols are generally weaker acids than water because alkyl electron donation destabilises the alkoxide conjugate base relative to hydroxide.

nodes.name: Oxidation of Alcohols
nodes.description: The oxidation of primary alcohols to aldehydes and carboxylic acids and secondary alcohols to ketones, with tertiary alcohols resistant.

nodes.name: Iodoform Test
nodes.description: Alcohols containing CH3CH(OH)- and carbonyl compounds containing CH3CO- give a yellow CHI3 precipitate with alkaline iodine, allowing the relevant structural group to be deduced from formulae or observations.

nodes.name: Aldehydes and Ketones
nodes.description: Carbonyl compounds containing a C=O group, undergoing nucleophilic addition and distinguished by oxidation and characteristic tests.

nodes.name: Carboxylic Acids
nodes.description: Organic acids containing the carboxyl group, showing acidic behaviour and reactions forming salts, esters, and acyl derivatives.

nodes.name: Esters and Acyl Chlorides
nodes.description: Esters form by condensation of acids and alcohols and can be hydrolysed. More reactive acyl chlorides undergo nucleophilic addition-elimination with water, alcohols, phenols, ammonia and amines through a tetrahedral intermediate.

nodes.name: Amines
nodes.description: Organic bases derived from ammonia, whose basicity arises from the nitrogen lone pair, along with their formation and reactions.

nodes.name: Amino Acids and Proteins
nodes.description: Amino acids bearing both amino and carboxyl groups, their zwitterion behaviour, and condensation into peptides and proteins.

nodes.name: Condensation Polymers
nodes.description: Condensation polymers such as polyesters and polyamides formed by joining monomers with loss of a small molecule like water.

nodes.name: Nitriles and Hydroxynitriles
nodes.description: Nitriles form from halogenoalkanes and ethanolic KCN, hydroxynitriles form by HCN addition to carbonyl compounds, and nitriles hydrolyse under heated dilute acid or alkali followed by acidification to give carboxylic acids.

nodes.name: Amides
nodes.description: Amides form when acyl chlorides react with ammonia or primary amines, hydrolyse in aqueous acid or alkali and can be reduced by LiAlH4; delocalisation of the nitrogen lone pair into the carbonyl makes amides much weaker bases than amines.

nodes.name: Benzene Structure
nodes.description: The structure of benzene as a planar ring with delocalised pi electrons, explaining its stability and resistance to addition reactions.

nodes.name: Electrophilic Substitution
nodes.description: Electrophilic substitution of arenes, including nitration and halogenation, in which an electrophile replaces a ring hydrogen.

nodes.name: Mass Spectrometry
nodes.description: Mass spectrometry determining relative molecular mass and structure from the mass-to-charge ratios of ionised molecular fragments.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot a mass spectrum of m/z peaks.

nodes.name: Phenol Preparation and Acid-Base Chemistry
nodes.name_zh: 苯酚的制备与酸碱性质
nodes.description: Phenol can be prepared by hydrolysing a diazonium salt, reacts with sodium and aqueous sodium hydroxide to form phenoxide, and is more acidic than water and ethanol because the phenoxide conjugate base is resonance-stabilised.

nodes.name: Phenol Ring Reactivity and Directing Effects
nodes.name_zh: 苯酚芳环反应与定位效应
nodes.description: The hydroxyl group activates the aromatic ring and directs electrophilic substitution to the 2-, 4- and 6-positions, so phenol nitrates and brominates under milder conditions than benzene; the same principles extend to phenolic compounds such as naphthol.

nodes.name: Diazonium Salts and Azo Compounds
nodes.description: Phenylamine forms a diazonium salt with nitrous acid below 10°C; the salt can hydrolyse to phenol or couple with phenol in alkaline solution to form compounds containing the -N=N- azo group, many of which are dyes.

nodes.name: Infrared Spectroscopy
nodes.description: Infrared spectroscopy identifying functional groups from the characteristic absorption of bonds vibrating at specific frequencies.

nodes.name: NMR Spectroscopy
nodes.description: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy determining molecular structure from the chemical environments of hydrogen or carbon nuclei.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot an NMR spectrum of chemical-shift peaks.

nodes.name: Chromatography
nodes.description: Chromatography separating mixtures by differential partition between a stationary and a mobile phase, characterised by Rf values or retention times.
